title: Cut 7 third judgment: the freeze's scope stated, in-scope findings fixed, the rest outside it
situation: The third judgment's rejecting assayer found routes past the freeze; most are deliberate tampering (hooks skipped, the ledger moved away, an integration written by hand, entries rewritten in place, commits replaced), which 0130 and 0131 put outside the freeze, though its wording had not said so. Three judgments have each found new routes of that kind.
decision: Fixed in this cut, each with its check seen red first: (1) what is frozen is read from the record (0132), the dispatch rule included; (2) widening a work package's outputs onto a file a frozen check uses is refused while the cut is frozen, and defining a concept a frozen cut names consults the freeze; (3) the history refuses any branch update that changes or deletes an existing journal entry, from anyone, since the journal is append-only; (4) the record point runs, and reads the freeze, in every work tree of the repository and on pushes into it, refusing where it cannot read. Outside the freeze, by its superseded wording and 0130 and 0131, and not findings against the work: skipped hooks, moving the ledger away, an integration written by hand, a set name, replaced commits. The cut is judged once more on that scope; findings outside it are recorded as hardening notes for the ipseic round.
consequences: The freeze checks are rebound for (1) to (4); the assayers are given 0130 to 0133 as the freeze's scope.
